o.text: From Proto-Turkic *bütün, a derivation of *büt- (“to end, accomplish; to create, build; to heal; to grow, ripen”), whence also Azerbaijani bütöv (“whole”).
Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish آرتمق (artmaq).
From dərs + -lik. Perhaps, calque of Russian учебник (učebnik).

From Persian سِدر (sedr), from French cèdre as if with Classical Persian vocalism. Alternatively, misread from Ottoman Turkish سِدْر, having the reading sedr from French cèdre and the reading sidr from Arabic سِدْر (sidr, “buckthorn”).
Borrowed from Arabic رُوحًا (rūḥan). By surface analysis, ruh + -ən.
